inputs.notes: Net debt from H1 FY2026 (most recent). Base FCF of NZ$14m represents a normalized estimate for FY2026, slightly above FY2025 actuals of NZ$12.9m and consistent with FY2026 operating profit guidance of NZ$20-24m at ~60-65% FCF conversion. FCF is projected using revenue-based approach (FCF margin expanding from 7% to 12%) rather than direct FCF CAGR due to the investment-phase suppression of near-term free cash flow.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR of 41.2% is not representative of sustainable growth - AFT only turned equity positive in FY2020 (recovering from negative equity). FCF CAGRs are negative due to deliberate R&D and international hub investment suppressing free cash flow. EPS is distorted by lumpy licensing income. Revenue CAGR (3yr: 16.9%, 5yr: 14.5%) is the most reliable indicator and is used as the primary growth anchor, per the user instruction to use revenue and FCF as primary drivers for AFT.

data_notes.fcf: FY2020: NZ$14.8m, FY2021: NZ$0.7m, FY2022: NZ$13.8m, FY2023: NZ$11.4m, FY2024: NZ$28.7m (includes licensing receipts), FY2025: NZ$12.9m
data_notes.h1_fy2026: Revenue NZ$114.9m (+33% vs H1 FY2025), Operating profit NZ$4.7m, NPAT NZ$2.7m

wacc_assumptions.rationale: 12% WACC reflects: (1) small-cap NZ listing with limited liquidity, (2) investment-phase with multiple international markets still pre-profitability, (3) NZD risk-free rate ~4.5%, (4) equity risk premium ~6-7%, (5) size/illiquidity premium ~1-2%. Bull case uses 10% as execution risk reduces with hub profitability. Bear case uses 14% to reflect extended investment period and execution risk materialising.
wacc_assumptions.terminal_growth_rationale: Base 3.0% reflects long-run nominal GDP growth of NZ/AU (~2.5-3%) plus pharmaceutical sector premium. Bull 3.5% reflects global expansion and recurring royalty stream compounding. Bear 2.0% reflects mature/slower growth with missed international targets.

base.narrative: Base case assumes AFT continues strong Australasian growth and approaches but does not fully achieve the NZ$300m FY2027 revenue target. International hubs (UK, South Africa) turn profitable in 2H FY2026 as guided. FCF margins expand from the current depressed level as R&D investment stabilises and hub losses convert to profits. Licensing income recovers modestly. By Year 5, revenue reaches ~NZ$417m with a 12% FCF margin, reflecting a more mature operating model.

bull.narrative: Bull case assumes the NZ$300m FY2027 revenue target is achieved and international hub scaling accelerates. Maxigesic IV gains strong hospital formulary traction in UK, Canada, and US (via Hikma). Licensing income recovers strongly in FY2026-FY2027 from the FY2025 trough, including meaningful milestones from the IV iron programme. FCF margins expand rapidly as international hubs become profitable. R&D pipeline delivers at least one significant out-licensing deal. By Year 5, revenue reaches ~NZ$482m with a 15% FCF margin.

bear.narrative: Bear case assumes international hub execution disappoints - UK and South Africa breakeven is delayed, Canada takes longer than guided, and the US Hikma partnership generates minimal revenue. Licensing income remains at low levels (no major milestones). Chemist Warehouse post-Sigma merger exerts pricing pressure on Australian margin. R&D spending remains elevated but pipeline advances slowly. Revenue growth decelerates sharply to mid-single digits by Year 3-4 as the Australasian market matures. FCF margins recover slowly as investment costs persist.

sensitivity.notes: Matrix shows base-case intrinsic value per share (NZD) across WACC (rows, 10-14%) and terminal growth rate (columns, 2.0-4.0%). Base assumptions are WACC=12%, terminal growth=3.0%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 25% bull / 50% base / 25% bear reflects balanced uncertainty. AFT has strong growth momentum (H1 FY2026 revenue +33%) and credible management, supporting equal probability of bull/bear tails. The base case aligned with company guidance and analyst consensus target of ~NZ$4.20 adds confidence to the 50% base weighting.

analyst_context.notes: Analyst consensus target of NZ$4.20 is broadly consistent with the base case DCF intrinsic value of NZ$3.97 and the probability-weighted value of NZ$4.42. Current price of NZ$3.40 trades at a 14-20% discount to base/weighted IV.
